### Difference Between Thermoplastic and Thermosetting Polymers

| Property | Thermoplastic Polymers | Thermosetting Polymers |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nature** | Soften on heating and stiffen on cooling reversibly. | Permanently set into a solid mass on heating; cannot be reshaped. |
| **Cross-linking** | Linear or branched chains held by weak Van der Waals forces. | Heavily cross-linked 3D network structure with covalent bonds. |
| **Reusability** | Can be repeatedly melted and recycled. | Cannot be recycled or remolded. |
| **Examples** | Polyethylene (PE), PVC, Polystyrene. | Bakelite, Urea-formaldehyde, Epoxy resins. |
proTip: Remember that thermoplastics undergo physical changes on heating, whereas thermosetting plastics undergo irreversible chemical cross-linking.
